# PV008 — Finance RAG evidence selection

Use only the supplied evidence catalog derived from a Form 10-K Item 1A packet. Identify exactly three distinct material risks based on the seriousness and breadth of consequences explicitly stated by the filer.

Each catalog record has an immutable header `[EVIDENCE ... | PDF_PAGE ... | PARAGRAPH ...]` followed by one exact physical source line. Select exactly one consequence-bearing `evidence_id` for each risk. Copy that ID exactly. Do not quote, rewrite, or generate source text; the deterministic locator will retrieve the corresponding frozen line after your response.

Return one JSON object only. Copy the harness `case_id`, `model_id`, and `prompt_version`. `risks` must contain exactly three objects with `risk_id` values `R1`, `R2`, `R3`. Every risk object must contain:

- string fields: `risk_id`, `risk_summary`, `risk_type`, `evidence_id`, `reasoning`, `financial_impact`, `time_horizon`, `mitigation`, `uncertainty`
- array of strings: `monitoring_indicators`

Use exactly one risk type: `Strategic / Market / Technology`, `Operational / Supply Chain`, `Regulatory / Legal / Geopolitical`, `Financial / Liquidity / Credit`, `Cybersecurity / Data / Privacy`, or `Other`.

Selection checks:

1. The chosen evidence ID must exist verbatim in the supplied catalog.
2. Its following source line must contain at least five words and state a risk cause, consequence, or financial/operating exposure—not merely a heading.
3. Use three different evidence IDs representing three distinct risk themes.
4. Base reasoning and financial impact on the selected source line and nearby catalog context only.

Do not invent controls, amounts, probabilities, forecasts, or plans. For this preparation round set `mitigation` exactly to `Not disclosed in the selected evidence line.` Keep every field concise.

Harness metadata (copy these values exactly into the top-level JSON):
- case_id: PYPL-FY24
- model_id: QuantFactory/Llama-3-8B-Instruct-Finance-RAG-GGUF:Q4_K_M
- prompt_version: PV008

Case: PYPL-FY24
Input view: deterministic evidence catalog derived from the frozen packet.
Every evidence record preserves one physical source line and its original locator.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0001 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P001]
legislative and regulatory landscapes with respect to cryptocurrency may subject us to additional licensing and regulatory obligations or to additional inquiries

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0002 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P001]
or investigations from the SEC or other regulators and governmental authorities, and require us to make product changes, restrict or discontinue product

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0003 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P001]
offerings in certain markets, implement additional and potentially costly controls, or take other actions.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0004 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
In August 2023, a third-party issuer with which we have partnered commercially (the “PYUSD Issuer”) launched a U.S. dollar-denominated stablecoin named

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0005 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
PayPal USD (“PYUSD”), which is available to PayPal U.S. customers and Venmo customers. These PayPal and Venmo customers may, if provisioned for

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0006 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
external transfers and subject to our sanctions and anti-money laundering controls, send PYUSD to external wallets not controlled by PayPal. The PYUSD

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0007 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
Issuer may also allow institutional users to directly purchase PYUSD from the PYUSD Issuer (as per the PYUSD Issuer’s stablecoin terms and conditions).

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0008 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
The regulatory treatment of stablecoins is evolving and has drawn significant attention from legislative and regulatory bodies around the world, including the

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0009 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
SEC. There are uncertainties on how ongoing changes to federal, state, and international laws and regulations would apply to stablecoins in practice, and we

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0010 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
and the PYUSD Issuer may face substantial costs to operationalize and comply with any additional or changed requirement. If we or the PYUSD Issuer fail to

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0011 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
comply with regulations, requirements, prohibitions or other obligations applicable to us, we could face regulatory or other enforcement actions, potential fines,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0012 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
penalties, and other consequences. In addition, we could face reputational harm through our relationship with the PYUSD Issuer if the PYUSD Issuer were to

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0013 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P002]
face regulatory scrutiny, PYUSD is deemed to be a security, or PYUSD is alleged to be used for transactions in connection with illicit or illegal activities.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0014 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P003]
We hold our customers’ cryptocurrency assets through one or more third-party custodians. Financial and third-party risks related to our customer

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0015 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P003]
cryptocurrency offerings, such as inappropriate access to, theft, or destruction of cryptocurrency assets held by our custodians, insufficient insurance coverage

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0016 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P003]
by a custodian to reimburse us for all such losses, a custodian’s failure to maintain effective controls over the custody and settlement services provided to us, a

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0017 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P003]
custodian’s inability to purchase or liquidate cryptocurrency holdings, the failure of the PYUSD Issuer to maintain sufficient reserve assets backing PYUSD

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0018 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P003]
and defaults on financial or performance obligations by a custodian, banks with which the PYUSD Issuer maintains reserve assets or counterparty financial

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0019 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P003]
institutions, could expose our customers and us to loss, and significantly harm our business, financial condition, and reputation.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0020 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P004]
We have selected custodian partners and the PYUSD Issuer, and may in the future select additional custodian partners and stablecoin issuing entities, that are

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0021 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P004]
subject to regulatory oversight, capital requirements, maintenance of audit and compliance industry certifications, and cybersecurity procedures and policies.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0022 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P004]
Nevertheless, any operational disruptions at any such custodian or issuer, or such custodians’ or issuer’s failure to safeguard cryptocurrency holdings (or

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0023 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P004]
reserve assets), could result in losses of customer assets, expose us to customer claims, reduce consumer confidence and materially impact our cryptocurrency

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0024 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P004]
product offerings and our operating results.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0025 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
Custodial arrangements to safeguard cryptocurrency assets involve unique risks and uncertainties in the event of a custodian’s bankruptcy. While other types of

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0026 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
assets and some custodied cryptocurrencies have been deemed not to be part of the custodian’s bankruptcy estate under various regulatory regimes, bankruptcy

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0027 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
courts have not yet definitively determined the appropriate treatment of custodial holdings of digital assets in a bankruptcy proceeding. In the event of a

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0028 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
custodian’s bankruptcy, the lack of precedent and the highly fact-dependent nature of the determination could delay or preclude the return of custodied

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0029 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
cryptocurrency assets to us or to our customers. Although we contractually require our custodians to segregate our customer assets and not commingle them

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0030 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
with proprietary or other assets, we cannot be certain that these contractual obligations, even if duly observed by a custodian, will be effective in preventing

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0031 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
such assets from being treated as part of the custodian’s estate under bankruptcy or other insolvency law. In that event, our claim on behalf of such customers

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0032 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
against a custodian’s estate for our customers’ cryptocurrency assets could be treated as a general unsecured claim against the custodian, in which case our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0033 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P005]
customers could seek to hold us liable for any resulting losses.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0034 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P006]
Lending Regulation

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0035 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P007]
We hold a number of U.S. state lending licenses for our U.S. consumer short-term installment loan product, which is subject to federal and state laws governing

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0036 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P007]
consumer credit and debt collection. Similarly, the consumer short-term installment loan products that we offer outside the U.S. may be subject to consumer

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0037 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P007]
credit legislation, licensing requirements, consumer lending laws, consumer protection or banking transparency regulations. Increased global regulatory focus

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0038 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P007]
on short-term installment products and consumer credit more broadly could result in laws or regulations requiring changes to our policies, procedures,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0039 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P007]
operations, and product offerings, and restrict or limit our ability to offer credit products.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0040 | PDF_PAGE 18 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P008]
Consumer Protection

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0041 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
property, there can be no assurance that we will be successful in protecting or enforcing our rights in every jurisdiction, that our contractual arrangements will

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0042 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
prevent or deter third parties from infringing or misappropriating our intellectual property, or that third parties will not independently develop equivalent or

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0043 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
superior intellectual property rights. We may be required to expend significant time and resources to prevent infringement and enforce our rights, and we may

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0044 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
be unable to discover or determine the extent of any unauthorized use of our proprietary rights. If we are unable to prevent third parties from infringing or

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0045 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
otherwise violating our proprietary rights, the uniqueness and value of our products and services could be adversely affected, the value of our brands could be

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0046 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
diminished, and our business could be adversely affected. We expect to continue to license in the future certain of our proprietary rights, such as trademarks or

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0047 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
copyrighted material, to others. These licensees may take actions that diminish the value of our proprietary rights or harm our reputation. Any failure to

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0048 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
adequately protect or enforce our proprietary rights, or significant costs incurred in doing so, could diminish the value of our intangible assets and materially

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0049 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P009]
harm our business.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0050 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P010]
BUSINESS AND OPERATIONS RISKS

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0051 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P011]
We face substantial and increasingly intense competition worldwide in the global payments industry.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0052 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P012]
The global payments industry is highly competitive, dynamic, and innovative, and increasingly subject to regulatory scrutiny and oversight. Many of the areas

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0053 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P012]
in which we compete evolve rapidly with innovative and disruptive technologies, shifting user preferences and needs, price sensitivity of consumers and

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0054 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P012]
merchants, and frequent introductions of new products and services. Competition also may intensify as new competitors emerge, businesses combine or enter

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0055 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P012]
into new partnerships, and established companies in other segments expand to become competitive with various aspects of our business.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0056 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
We compete with a wide range of businesses in every aspect of our business. Some of our current and potential competitors are or may be larger than we are,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0057 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
have larger customer bases, greater brand recognition, longer operating histories, a dominant or more secure position, broader geographic scope, volume, scale,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0058 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
resources, and market share than we do, or offer products and services that we do not offer. Other competitors are or may be smaller or younger companies that

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0059 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
may be more agile in responding to regulatory and technological changes and customer preferences. Our competitors may devote greater resources to the

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0060 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
development, promotion, and sale of products and services, and/or offer lower prices or more effectively offer their own innovative programs, products, and

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0061 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
services. We often partner with other businesses, and the ability to continue developing these partnerships is important to our business. Competition for

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0062 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
relationships with these partners is intense, and there can be no assurance that we will be able to continue to establish, grow, or maintain these partner

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0063 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
relationships. If we are unable to differentiate our products and services from those of our competitors, drive value for our customers and adoption of our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0064 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
products and services, or effectively and efficiently align our resources with our goals and objectives, we may not be able to compete effectively, which could

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0065 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P013]
negatively impact our results of operations and financial condition.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0066 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P014]
Changes to payment card networks or bank fees, rules, or practices could harm our business.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0067 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
To process certain transactions, we must comply with applicable payment card, bank or other network (collectively, “network”) rules. The rules govern all

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0068 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
aspects of a transaction on the networks, including fees and other practices. From time to time, the networks have increased the fees and assessments that they

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0069 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
charge for transactions that access their networks. Certain networks have also imposed special fees or assessments for transactions that are executed through a

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0070 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
digital wallet such as the one that PayPal offers. Our payment processors may have the right to pass any increases in fees and assessments on to us and to

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0071 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
increase their own fees for processing. Any increase in interchange fees, special fees, or assessments for transactions that we pay to the networks or our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0072 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
payment processors could make our pricing less competitive, increase our operating costs, and reduce our operating income, which could materially harm our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0073 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P015]
business, financial condition, and results of operations.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0074 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P016]
In some jurisdictions, government regulations have required payment card networks to reduce or cap interchange fees. Any changes in interchange fee rates or

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0075 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P016]
limitations, or their applicability to PayPal’s products and services, could adversely affect our competitive position against payment card service providers and

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0076 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P016]
the revenue we earn from our branded card programs, require us to change our business practices, and harm our business.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0077 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P017]
We may also be subject to fines and other penalties assessed by networks resulting from any rule violations by us or our merchants. The networks set and

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0078 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P017]
interpret their rules, and have alleged from time to time that various aspects of our business model violate these rules, or our agreements with the networks.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0079 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P017]
Such allegations may result in significant fines, penalties, damages, or other liabilities, adversely impact benefits to us under the agreements, or require changes

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0080 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P017]
in our business practices that may be costly and adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition. The network rules may also

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0081 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P017]
increase the cost of, impose restrictions on, or otherwise impact the development of, our products which may negatively affect product deployment and

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0082 | PDF_PAGE 21 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P017]
adoption. The networks could adopt new operating rules or interpret or re-interpret existing rules that

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0083 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P018]
we or our payment processors might find difficult or impractical to follow, or costly to implement, which could require us to make significant changes to our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0084 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P018]
products, increase our operational costs, and negatively impact our business. If we become unable or limited in our ability to accept certain payment types such

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0085 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P018]
as debit or credit cards, our business would be materially and adversely affected.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0086 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P019]
Changes in how consumers fund their PayPal transactions could harm our business.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0087 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
We pay transaction fees when consumers fund payment transactions using credit cards, lower fees when consumers fund payments with debit cards, and

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0088 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
nominal fees when consumers fund payment transactions by electronic transfer of funds from bank accounts, from an existing PayPal account balance or

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0089 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
Venmo account balance, or through our PayPal branded consumer credit products. Our financial performance is sensitive to changes in the rate at which our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0090 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
consumers fund payments using payment cards, which can significantly increase our costs. Although we provide consumers in certain markets with the

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0091 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
opportunity to use their existing PayPal account balance or Venmo account balance to fund payment transactions, some of our consumers may prefer to use

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0092 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
payment cards, which may offer features and benefits not provided as part of their PayPal accounts. Any increase in the portion of our payment volume funded

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0093 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
using payment cards or in fees associated with our funding mix, or other events or developments that make it more difficult or costly for us to fund transactions

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0094 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P020]
with lower-cost funding options, could materially and adversely affect our financial performance and significantly harm our business.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0095 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P021]
Our credit products expose us to additional risks.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0096 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
We offer credit products to a wide range of consumers and merchants in the U.S. and various international markets. The financial success of these products

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0097 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
depends largely on the effective management of related risk. The credit decision-making process for our consumer credit products uses proprietary

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0098 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
methodologies and credit algorithms and other analytical techniques designed to analyze the credit risk of specific consumers based on, among other factors,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0099 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
their past purchase and transaction history with PayPal or Venmo and their credit scores. Similarly, proprietary risk models and other indicators are applied to

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0100 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
assess merchants who desire to use our merchant financing offerings to help predict their ability to repay. These risk models may not accurately predict the

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0101 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
creditworthiness of a consumer or merchant due to inaccurate assumptions, including those related to the particular consumer or merchant, market conditions,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0102 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
economic environment, or limited transaction history or other data. The accuracy of these risk models and the ability to manage credit risk related to our credit

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0103 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
products may also be affected by legal or regulatory requirements, changes in consumer behavior, changes in the economic environment, issuing bank policies,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0104 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P022]
and other factors.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0105 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
We are subject to the risk that account holders who use our credit products will default on their payment obligations. The non-payment rate among account

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0106 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
holders may increase due to, among other factors, changes to underwriting standards, risk models not accurately predicting the creditworthiness of a user,

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0107 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
worsening economic conditions, such as a recession or government austerity programs, increases in prevailing interest rates, and high unemployment rates.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0108 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
Account holders who miss payments often fail to repay their loans, and account holders who file for protection under the bankruptcy laws generally do not

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0109 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
repay their loans. Further, laws or regulations may limit the assessment of late fees or penalties on certain credit products, which could negatively impact our

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0110 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
revenue share arrangement with an independent chartered financial institution with respect to our U.S. consumer credit products. Any deterioration in the

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0111 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
performance of loans facilitated through our platform or unexpected losses on such loans may increase the risk of potential charge-offs, increase our allowance

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0112 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
for loans and interest receivable, negatively impact our revenue share arrangement (as discussed in “Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0113 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
Financial Condition and Results of Operations — Key Metrics and Financial Results”), and materially and adversely affect our financial condition and results

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0114 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P023]
of operations.

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0115 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P024]
We generally rely on the activities and charters of unaffiliated financial institutions to provide PayPal and Venmo branded consumer credit and merchant

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0116 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P024]
financing offerings to our U.S. customers. As a service provider to these unaffiliated financial institutions, which are federally supervised U.S. financial

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0117 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P024]
institutions, we are subject from time to time to examination by their federal banking regulators. In the event of any termination or interruption in a partner

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0118 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P024]
bank’s ability or willingness to lend, our ability to offer consumer credit and merchant financing products could be interrupted or limited, which could

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0119 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P024]
materially and adversely affect our business. We may be unable to reach a similar arrangement with another unaffiliated financial institution on favorable terms

[EVIDENCE PYPL-FY24-E0120 | PDF_PAGE 22 | PARAGRAPH PYPL-FY24-P024]
or at all. Obtaining and maintaining the lending licenses required for us to originate such loans ourselves would be a costly, time-consuming and uncertain
